title: DidactComponentDescriptor
description: Declarative schema skeleton for describing a Didact component, inspired by H5P semantics.json's dual pattern (research.md 9.2): the same document is used to generate prop documentation/editor AND to validate at runtime. This is not the registry's own registry-item.json (that lives in @didact/registry) -- this schema describes the component's own PROPS, with the RNF-4 detail (props that may arrive incomplete in streaming contexts).

requirementId.description: requirements.md functional requirement ID this component satisfies, e.g. 'RF-1'.

qtiInteraction.description: Equivalent QTI 3.0 interaction, if applicable (see validators/pedagogy/qti-mapping.json). null if not applicable (e.g. Flashcard is not an assessment interaction).

xapiInteractionType.description: Equivalent xAPI interactionType, if applicable (see validators/pedagogy/xapi-mapping.json).

wcagCriteria.description: IDs of the WCAG 2.2 criteria this component must meet (see validators/a11y/wcag-criteria.json), e.g. ['2.5.7', '2.4.7'].

props.description: List of the component's typed props.

type.description: Prop type. 'node' for React content/slots (e.g. RF-4/RF-6's informative feedback slot, see validators/pedagogy/README.md).

enumValues.description: Only if type is 'enum': the allowed values.

default.description: Default value for the prop, if it has one. Can be any JSON type.

requiredness.description: 'required': must always be present. 'progressive': may arrive absent in an incomplete render (RNF-4, streaming context) and the component must degrade gracefully (e.g. a loading state). 'optional': never mandatory, has reasonable default behavior if missing.

description.description: Natural-language explanation of what the prop is for, meant for someone reading the registry without opening the source code (design.md 8: 'the registry must be enough to understand what the CLI copies without reading the source code first').
